sets.title: Pie Chart + Table - Yoga Classes
sets.context:
There are three types of classes: Basic, Regular and Advance, of duration 1 hour, 2 hours and 3 hours respectively.
A pie chart gives the percentage of class time (in hours) taken by four yoga teachers. Total time for classes in a month = 450 hours.
(Pie-chart shares reconstructed from the answer key: Aditya 22%, Vaibhav 28%, Vishnu 16%, Sachin 34%.)

The table gives the ratio of time spent on the different types of classes by each teacher:

| Teacher | 1 Hour Class | 2 Hour Class | 3 Hour Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aditya | 5 | 4 | 2 |
| Vaibhav | 2 | 7 | 5 |
| Vishnu | 1 | 2 | 6 |
| Sachin | 6 | 8 | 3 |

sets.title: Five Writers and Their Friends
sets.context:
There are 5 different writers: A, B, C, D and E. They write books and distribute them among their friends. None of these friends are mutual (no friend is shared). Also:
(i) A has 7 friends. Each of his friends has 4 friends.
(ii) B has 5 friends. Each of his friends has 3 friends.
(iii) C has 4 friends. Each of his friends has 5 friends.
(iv) D has 6 friends. Each of his friends has 2 friends.
(v) E has 3 friends. Each of his friends has 5 friends.

questions.question: What is the percentage of the number of basic classes taken by Vaibhav sir to the number of regular classes taken by Sachin sir?
questions.explanation: Vaibhav's hours = 28% of 450 = 126; basic time = 2/14 x 126 = 18 h = 18 classes (1 h each). Sachin's hours = 34% of 450 = 153; regular time = 8/17 x 153 = 72 h = 36 classes (2 h each). 18/36 = 50%.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: How many more regular classes were taken by Aditya sir than the advance classes taken by Vaibhav sir?
questions.explanation: Aditya's hours = 22% of 450 = 99; regular time = 4/11 x 99 = 36 h = 18 classes. Vaibhav's advance time = 5/14 x 126 = 45 h = 15 classes (3 h each). Difference = 18 - 15 = 3.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: What is the ratio of the time spent by Sachin sir and Vishnu sir together in basic level classes to that of the regular level classes through the month?
questions.explanation: Sachin: basic 6/17 x 153 = 54 h, regular 8/17 x 153 = 72 h. Vishnu (16% of 450 = 72 h): basic 1/9 x 72 = 8 h, regular 2/9 x 72 = 16 h. Basic total 62 h, regular total 88 h; 62 : 88 = 31 : 44.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: Find the ratio of the number of basic classes of Vaibhav sir to the number of advance classes taken by Vishnu sir in the given period of time.
questions.explanation: Vaibhav's basic classes = 2/14 x 126 = 18 h = 18 classes. Vishnu's advance time = 6/9 x 72 = 48 h = 16 classes (3 h each). Ratio 18 : 16 = 9 : 8.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: E has written 300 books, distributed equally among his friends. Each of his friends further distributes an equal number of books to his/her friends. Among E's friends, 1 is male and the rest are females. If the male friend of E can distribute a maximum of 60 books to his female friends, find the maximum possible number of female friends of the male friend of E.
questions.explanation: E's 3 friends get 100 books each; each has 5 friends, so each friend of a friend gets 100/5 = 20 books. With at most 60 books going to female friends, the male friend can have at most 60/20 = 3 female friends.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: E has written 300 books, distributed equally among his friends, and each friend further distributes an equal number of books to his/her friends. Among E's friends, 1 is male and the remaining are females. In how many ways can the female friends of E distribute 1 book more to their friends than the male friend does?
questions.explanation: The book's key gives 120. Each of E's friends holds 100 books for 5 friends (20 each); counting the arrangements in which each of the two female friends passes on one book more than the male friend does yields 120 ways as per the key. The printed statement is garbled, so the exact intended counting cannot be reconstructed with certainty.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: C has written 400 books and D has written 600 books, distributed equally among their respective friends. The friends of C do not distribute these books further, but the friends of D distribute the books they received among their respective friends. What will be the average of the number of books received by each friend of C and the number received by each friend of the friends of D?
questions.explanation: Each of C's 4 friends gets 400/4 = 100 books. Each of D's 6 friends gets 100 books and passes them to 2 friends, 50 each. Average = (100 + 50)/2 = 75.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: A has written 700 books and B has written 450 books, distributed equally among their respective friends. Their friends then distribute the books they received among their own friends. By what percentage is the number of books received by the friends of the friends of B more than those received by the friends of the friends of A?
questions.explanation: A: 700/7 = 100 books per friend, then 100/4 = 25 per friend-of-friend. B: 450/5 = 90 per friend, then 90/3 = 30 per friend-of-friend. 30 is 20% more than 25.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: In how many ways can the friends of A exchange their 1 book with each other?
questions.explanation: A has 7 friends and each of them has 4 friends of his own (none mutual). Each of the 7 friends can exchange a book with each of his 4 friends, giving 7 x 4 = 28 exchanges.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2021 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)
